questions.question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object in the road.
questions.explanation: Be cautious when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road. Always drive carefully around bicyclists.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are the best choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season and requires extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires give better grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can cross solid yellow lines only when you are turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that pedestrians cross here. Watch for people crossing in front of you. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean you must stop. Give the right-of-way to other drivers. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing.
After one train passes, look for another train on the other track.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, look for another train on the other track.
questions.explanation: When two tracks run side by side, a second train may come after the first one passes. Check both tracks before crossing. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Honk at incoming traffic.
Always keep your current speed.
Speed up to avoid traffic.
Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: On roads with two or more lanes, make room for vehicles entering the road. If the lane next to you is empty, move over to let traffic in.

questions.question: What is a "No zone?"

options.text: A designated no passing zone.
A one-way traffic area.
The blind spot of a large vehicle.
An area for motor vehicles only.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks and large vehicles. Avoid staying in these areas where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When an oncoming car has bright headlights shining at you, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If bright headlights are coming at you, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic flows in both directions ahead.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
A construction area is ahead.
You must turn left soon.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line marks the edge of the road. When this line angles toward the center, the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Follow other cars more closely.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, do not make sudden changes in speed or direction. Reduce your speed and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels straight.
Leave the transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. If your car rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What do downward-pointing triangle signs mean?

options.text: School zone ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-pointing triangle signs tell drivers to yield. You may proceed when the road is clear and safe.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much alcohol you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. It is not affected by your fitness level.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
Multiple curves are ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes especially slippery in wet conditions.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because few other cars are coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the road.
When your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves—you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not pass by using the shoulder. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same way you do on dry roads.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase your following distance. Your car will need more time to stop than on dry roads.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert around motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and harder to spot than larger vehicles. Drivers must stay alert to prevent collisions with these smaller road users.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop until you know it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on an upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.
Trucks are on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill or downgrade is ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Lanes move in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Lanes move in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Lanes move in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means drivers cannot pass.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly to give approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to get out of your way.
Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. Failing to stop is illegal.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means drivers in both directions can pass if it is safe. Only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Another driver is trying to pass your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing vehicle can safely move back into your lane.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass even if it is dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look, and proceed with care.

questions.question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, a driver should:

options.text: Keep the same speed and proceed.
Stop, look in all directions, and proceed.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles approaching from the right. Always be ready to yield to prevent a crash. Release the accelerator, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: When driving past a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Expect the driver to open the car door as you pass.
Speed up.
Brake hard.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the car door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a vehicle that just parked, expect the driver to open the door as you approach. Use extra caution around parked vehicles.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, drivers must stop within ____ of the first rail when instructed to do so.

options.text: 70 feet
50 feet
15 feet
5 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: Drivers and pedestrians must stop within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet, from the nearest rail when warning lights flash, gates lower, or you are instructed to stop.
